reuse.why: Routes every expected-amount site through the existing exported getScheduledAmount and builds the approximate case on the existing getApproxNumberThreshold instead of recomputing the 7.5% tolerance.

duplication.why: Removes five hand-written midpoint/missing-amount ternaries (forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview, schedule-template) in favour of the one helper, and adds no new copies.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the other schedule amount/date helpers, the API only decorates its list output, and server and client callers just pass their raw amount and operator.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; the only noise is release notes that are stale or placeholder (step 1's note says 'largest expected amount' and has author 'YourGitHubUsername').

maintainability.why: A future change to the planning rule is a one-function edit with tests; the operator is now an explicit parameter and the missing/number/range/approx dispatch is in one place.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No site keeps its own computation; all former inline copies now call getScheduledAmount

disguised_duplication.where: Former copies were deleted, not reshaped

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an `amountOp` parameter (inverse moved to third position, no caller used it) and one `isapprox` branch that is the requested rule itself; no call site bypasses it after the change (useScheduleEdit's operator-switch conversion is a separate UI concern)
